title: Screen shield

status.insecure: This build uses an insecure service address, so the shield is off.
status.on: On. Tap the doll on anything suspicious.
status.off: Off. Turn it on to check what is on your screen.

steps.overlay: Step 1 of 4: allow "Display over other apps", then come back to $t(common:appName).
steps.notifications: Step 2 of 4: allow notifications so Android keeps the shield running.
steps.capture: Step 3 of 4: allow $t(common:appName) to see your screen when you tap the doll.

needs.title: What the shield needs
needs.overlay: Allow "Display over other apps" so the doll can float over other apps.
needs.notifications: Allow notifications so Android keeps the shield running.
needs.capture: Allow screen capture. $t(common:appName) only looks at your screen when you tap the doll.
needs.privacy: The screenshot goes to the check service only to be checked. It is not saved.

body: A small Pyit Taing Htaung doll floats over other apps. Tap it on a job post, chat or listing and $t(common:appName) checks what is on your screen.

errors.needsScreen: The shield needs to see your screen to check it. Try again and tap Start now.
errors.notStarted: The shield did not start. Check that "Display over other apps" is allowed and try again.
errors.failed: The shield did not start. Try again.
errors.checkFailed: The check did not start. Turn the shield on and try again.

messageGuard.title: Message Guard: warns you about risky messages as they arrive
messageGuard.privacy: Off unless you turn it on. Only messages that look risky leave your phone, with names, numbers and codes removed first.

status.on: On. Messages from the apps you chose that look risky get a quiet notice.
status.needsAccess: Off. Turning it on first explains what it reads.
status.paused: Paused. It reached 60 checks in one day, the most it allows. Turn it on again to resume.

errors.accessOff: Notification access is still off. If the switch is greyed out, open $t(common:appName) in App info, tap the three dots and choose "Allow restricted settings".
errors.cannotOpen: Could not open the notification access settings.

consent.title: Before you turn on Message Guard

reads.title: What it reads
reads.body: New notifications from the apps you choose below. It does not read any other app.

leaves.title: What leaves your phone
leaves.body: Only messages that look risky. Numbers, emails, codes, names and the parts of links after the website name are removed first.

never.title: What never leaves your phone
never.body: One-time codes (OTP), who sent the message, and every message that does not look risky.

who.title: Who checks it
who.body: $t(common:appName)'s server and Google's AI check the message and send back a result.

control.title: You stay in control
control.body: You can turn it off at any time. "What Message Guard sent" shows every message it sent.

phone.title: Others may see notices
phone.body: Anyone who holds your phone may see $t(common:appName) notices and results.

consent.addBody: Message Guard will also read new notifications from {{app}}. Everything below stays the same.

log.title: What Message Guard sent
log.body: The exact text that left your phone. It is kept only on this phone, for 7 days.

kill.label: Turn off and remove access
kill.hint: Turns Message Guard off and opens Android settings, where you can remove $t(common:appName)'s notification access.

notice.body: A message may need a second look. Open to see why.

activity.waiting: Waiting for messages from the apps you chose.

outcome.paused: not checked, Message Guard is paused
outcome.hiddenPreview: the app hid the text, so it could not be checked. Turn on message previews in that app.
outcome.tooShort: too short to check, not sent
outcome.otp: a one-time code, kept on your phone
outcome.duplicate: same as a recent message, not sent again
outcome.rateLimited: not sent, the hourly or daily limit is reached
outcome.sent: sent for a check, waiting for the result
outcome.checkFailed: the check did not finish. Check your internet connection.
outcome.noticeBlocked: checked, but $t(common:appName) notifications are off, so the notice did not show

health.accessOff: Notification access is off, so Message Guard cannot read new messages.
health.notConnected: Android has not started Message Guard yet. Turn it off and on again, or restart the phone.
health.notificationsOff: $t(common:appName) notifications are off, so you will not see warnings.
health.battery: Android may stop Message Guard to save battery.
